figure: FIGURE 15.2, panel (a) 'Caching removes prefill work' — in-plot note f(r)=(1-S+P)/S
issue: The formula printed inside panel (a) does not reproduce the curve drawn in that panel, and the caption repeats the same formula. As rendered, the note reads f(r)=(1-S+P)/S with P=40% and S=60%. Substitution gives f(1) = (1-0.60+0.40)/0.60 = 0.80/0.60 = 1.333, i.e. 133 GFLOPs at r=1, whereas the drawn green curve starts at exactly 100 (the no-cache value) at r=1 and ends near 60-64 at r=10. The drawn series is reproduced by f(r) = S + P/r = 0.60 + 0.40/r (f(1)=1.00, f(2)=0.80, f(5)=0.68, f(10)=0.64), which is the only formula family consistent with the caption's own definitions ('P = 40% - the reusable prefix share of the prompt - and S = 60% - the unique suffix'). As printed, the note is wrong at every plotted point, and the caption's gloss 'the in-plot note's f(r)=(1-S+P)/S' propagates the error into the prose. (The exact glyphs must be confirmed against the figure source: if the source string contains an '/r' term, the same defect persists, because (1-S+P/r)/S = 1.333 at r=1.)
evidence: Recomputation from the page's own stated inputs: P=0.40, S=0.60. Printed formula: f(1) = (1-0.6+0.4)/0.6 = 1.333 -> 133 GFLOPs; f(10) = (1-0.6+0.4)/0.6 = 1.333 (no r dependence at all as read). Drawn curve: f(1) = 1.00 (100 GFLOPs, coincident with the flat 'no cache' series), f(10) ~= 0.60-0.64. Candidate correct form S + P/r: f(1)=1.00, f(2)=0.80, f(3)=0.733, f(5)=0.68, f(8)=0.65, f(10)=0.64 - matching the drawn curve's steep initial drop and its flattening toward ~0.62. The caption's own definition of reuse ('mean number of requests served from each cached prefix block, so 1 = no sharing and hence no prefix reduction') also requires f(1)=1, which the printed formula violates.
acceptance_test: Extract the exact note string from the figure source; recompute f(1), f(2), f(5), f(10) with P=0.40, S=0.60; confirm the plotted series equals the printed formula at all four points. If not, replace the note with f(r) = S + P/r (or (S*r + P)/r), update the caption gloss accordingly, and re-verify that the caption's '1 = no sharing and hence no prefix reduction' statement holds at r=1.

figure: FIGURE 15.2, panel (a) y-axis label 'Prefill FLOPs / req (G)'
issue: The left panel's y-axis is labeled in absolute units ('Prefill FLOPs / req (G)', 0-100) while the caption describes the same panel as 'prefill work vs average prefix reuse, as a percent of no-cache prefill work'. The two cannot both be true. As an absolute value the axis is also implausible: 100 GFLOPs of prefill per request corresponds to roughly 7 prompt tokens on a 7B model (2*N*T = 1.4e10*T) and to 0.7 tokens on a 70B model, so no realistic model/prompt pair yields a 100 GFLOPs prefill baseline. The plotted quantity is therefore a normalized ratio, and the axis label misrepresents it as an absolute cost. A reader who trusts the axis could conclude that prefill is trivially cheap and therefore never compute-bound - the exact misconception the surrounding chapter is trying to prevent.
evidence: Caption text on the page: 'left: prefill work vs average prefix reuse, as a percent of no-cache prefill work, lower is better'. Axis text: 'Prefill FLOPs / req (G)' with the 'no cache' series flat at 100. Prefill FLOPs check: 2 * 7e9 * T = 100e9 -> T ~= 7.1 tokens; 2 * 70e9 * T = 100e9 -> T ~= 0.71 tokens. Both are far below any realistic prompt length, confirming the axis is normalized, not absolute. The '(G)' suffix is also ambiguous between 'giga' and 'GFLOP'.
acceptance_test: Relabel the axis 'Prefill work per request (% of no-cache)' (dropping '(G)'), or state the absolute baseline in the caption (e.g. 'no-cache prefill = X GFLOPs for the canonical model and prompt') and verify X against the book's canonical workload. Confirm the caption and axis then describe the same quantity.

figure: FIGURE 15.2, caption clause 'caching raises decode goodput (right: decode goodput vs batch size, ...)'
issue: The caption attributes the right-hand panel to caching, while the panel's own x-axis is 'Decode batch size' and the body text on the same page attributes it to batching: 'batching raises decode goodput (right plot) until bandwidth saturates, while prefix caching lowers the prefill work per repeated prompt (left plot)'. If the caption string is 'caching', the caption contradicts its own parenthetical, contradicts the prose, and teaches the reader that prefix caching raises decode goodput - a claim the figure cannot support and that the book's own lever separation (left = prefill phase, right = decode phase) is designed to prevent. The figure title ('Prefill caching vs batching: two independent effects') and the panel titles are consistent with the prose, so the caption is the odd element out.
evidence: Caption: '...; caching raises decode goodput (right: decode goodput vs batch size, arbitrary goodput units, rising with diminishing gains as HBM bandwidth approaches saturation ...)'. Body text, same page: 'batching raises decode goodput (right plot) until bandwidth saturates, while prefix caching lowers the prefill work per repeated prompt (left plot)'. Panel (b) x-axis: 'Decode batch size'. No caching variable appears on the right panel's axes.
acceptance_test: Grep the caption source for 'raises decode goodput' and confirm the grammatical subject is 'batching'. If it is 'caching', change it to 'batching' and re-verify that the caption's two-lever mapping (left = prefix caching, right = batching) matches both panel titles and the prose paragraph.

figure: FIGURE 15.2, panel (a) title 'Caching removes prefill work'
issue: The panel title asserts elimination, but the drawn curve has a nonzero floor: the green series asymptotes at roughly 60-64 GFLOPs, i.e. 36-40% of the no-cache prefill work survives even at r=10, because the unique suffix (S=60%) is never cached. The caption's own wording ('prefix caching cuts prefill work per repeated prompt') is the accurate one; the panel title overstates it.
evidence: Drawn green series: f(10) ~= 0.60-0.64 of the no-cache value, consistent with the floor S = 0.60 imposed by the uncacheable suffix. Panel title: 'Caching removes prefill work'.
acceptance_test: Retitle panel (a) to 'Prefix caching cuts prefill work' (or 'Caching removes the shared prefix's prefill work'); confirm the title asserts reduction, not elimination, and that it agrees with the caption's verb.

figure: FIGURE 15.2, panel (b) y-axis label 'Relative decode goodput (a.u.)'
issue: 'Relative' has no stated base and neither plausible base matches the drawn curve. If the series were normalized to batch size 1, the b=1 point would read 100; it reads about 5. If it were normalized to the peak, the b=10 point would read 100; it reads about 90. The caption supplies only 'arbitrary goodput units', so the axis mixes two conventions ('relative' and 'arbitrary') without defining either.

acceptance_test: Either drop 'Relative' ('Decode goodput (arbitrary units)') or state the base explicitly ('normalized to the b=10 point'); confirm the stated base reproduces the drawn endpoint values.

figure: FIGURE 15.2, figure title 'Prefill caching vs batching: two independent effects'
issue: The figure title introduces 'prefill caching', a third caching term, on a page whose caption and prose use 'prefix caching'. The book elsewhere treats prefix caching, prompt caching, and KV caching as distinct concepts with distinct scopes; adding 'prefill caching' in a prominent heading risks the reader treating it as a fourth mechanism or as a synonym for one of the existing three.
evidence: Figure title: 'Prefill caching vs batching: two independent effects'. Caption on the same page: 'prefix caching cuts prefill work per repeated prompt'. Body text: 'prefix caching lowers the prefill work per repeated prompt (left plot)'.
acceptance_test: Rename the figure title to 'Prefix caching vs batching: ...' (or 'Caching the prefill phase vs batching the decode phase'); grep the manuscript for remaining 'prefill caching' occurrences and confirm each is either defined or replaced.

figure: FIGURE 15.2, panel (b) red annotation block and x-axis ticks
issue: The red annotation ('diminishing gains / past ~b=6 (no hard / plateau); goodput units / still rise; tail / latency keeps rising') is the smallest glyph set in the figure, is set inside the plot area immediately to the left of the dashed b~6 line, and its lower lines sit at the same vertical band as the rising curve near b=5-7, so the reader must decode a six-line parenthetical in the tightest region of the panel. The x-axis carries only the labels 1 and 10, so the referenced b=6 cannot be located from ticks alone; the reader must infer it from the dashed line's position.

figure: FIGURE 15.2, figure title ('two independent effects') and the body paragraph immediately below the caption
issue: The independence claim is stronger than the page's own reasoning supports. The figure title says 'two independent effects' and the body text says 'They are not competing on the same axis: the decode bottleneck is unaffected by caching.' But the same paragraph states that caching leaves 'more prefill-recompute headroom ... under the same host'. Under continuous batching, freed prefill headroom changes how many sequences can be resident, which changes the decode batch size - precisely the quantity on the right panel's x-axis. The levers act on different phases (which is the correct framing), but they are not independent and the decode bottleneck is indirectly affected.
evidence: Body text on the page: 'batching raises decode goodput (right plot) until bandwidth saturates, while prefix caching lowers the prefill work per repeated prompt (left plot) so more prefill-recompute headroom remains under the same host. They are not competing on the same axis: the decode bottleneck is unaffected by caching.' Figure title: 'Prefill caching vs batching: two independent effects'.
acceptance_test: Reword to something like 'the two levers act on different phases: caching changes prefill-phase cost and, indirectly, the concurrency available to the decode phase; batching changes the decode-phase batch size directly'; remove 'independent' from the figure title and confirm the revised claim is consistent with the continuous-batching discussion elsewhere in the chapter.

figure: TCO break-even figure (referenced in prose as "the figure"; figure itself NOT on this page or p. 291 — see FIG-291-04)
issue: The break-even arithmetic that defines the figure's break-even band is typeset with the wrong operator. As rendered, the clause reads "6,232,677.2 = 155,816.93 × 0.025" and "10,387,795.33 = 155,816.93 × 0.015". Multiplication gives 3,895.42 and 2,337.25, not the printed results. The printed results are exactly the QUOTIENTS (155,816.93 ÷ 0.025 = 6,232,677.2; 155,816.93 ÷ 0.015 = 10,387,795.33), i.e. break-even requests/month = monthly cost ÷ cost per request. The same operator appears in the 22-host clause ("6,510,426.6 = 162,760.59 × 0.025") and in the 70%×95% clause ("232,197.23 × 0.0208 = … 11.2M req/mo"). If the source glyph is actually "÷" and only the 150 dpi render is ambiguous, this is a false positive — but if the source says "×", the entire break-even derivation (the 6.2–10.4M band and the 7.5M canonical point that the figure plots) is arithmetically wrong as printed.
evidence: Recomputed from the page's own inputs: 155,816.93 ÷ 0.025 = 6,232,677.2 (printed value matches to 7 s.f.); 155,816.93 ÷ 0.015 = 10,387,795.33 (matches); 155,816.93 ÷ 0.0208 = 7,491,198.56 (matches the printed canonical point); 162,760.59 ÷ 0.025 = 6,510,423.6 vs printed 6,510,426.6 (Δ = 3.0, i.e. 5e-5 relative — rounding of the unrounded monthly cost, not a finding); 162,760.59 ÷ 0.0208 = 7,825,028.4 (matches printed 7,825,028); 232,197.23 ÷ 0.0208 = 11,163,328 ≈ 11.2M (matches printed). Every printed RESULT is a quotient; no printed result is a product. Multiplication by the same factors yields values off by 1,600× and 4,444× respectively.
acceptance_test: Open the source for printed p. 270 and confirm the glyph. If it is "×", replace with "÷" in all four instances (21-host low end, 21-host high end, 22-host low end, 70%×95% case) and re-verify that each printed result still equals cost ÷ price-per-request. Then confirm the figure's break-even band endpoints (6.2M and 10.4M) and its canonical-price marker (7.5M at $0.0208) are unchanged and still consistent with the corrected equations.

issue: Two clauses in the same paragraph appear to have lost an operand at the 150 dpi render, leaving dangling fragments that make the derivation unreadable: (a) the 22-host clause renders as "6,510,426.6 = 162,760.59 × 0.025 = 0.015, canonical-price point 7,825,028 = 7.8M …" — the high-end product for the $0.015/request price is missing, so the reader sees "= 0.015" with nothing on its left; (b) the 70%×95% clause renders as "gives 232,197.23 × 0.0208 = 0.0208 = 11.2M req/mo", which contains a duplicated "= 0.0208" fragment. Either the source has dropped terms (a real defect) or the render has dropped them (a false positive). Either way the sentence as it currently reads cannot be followed.
evidence: Expected values if the intended chain is complete: 22-host high end = 162,760.59 ÷ 0.015 = 10,850,706 (a plausible missing term); 70%×95% case = 232,197.23 ÷ 0.0208 = 11,163,328 = 11.2M (a plausible missing term). The printed "= 11.2M req/mo" is consistent with the quotient, not the product.
acceptance_test: Read the source lines for printed p. 270 and confirm whether the terms 10,850,706 and 11,163,328 are present. If absent, restore them so that each clause reads as a complete chain (cost ÷ price = volume = rounded value). Re-render at 300 dpi and confirm no clause ends with a bare "= 0.015" or repeats "= 0.0208".

figure: TCO break-even / feasible-volume figure (referenced three times as "the figure")

The reader on printed p. 270 is told "the figure marks the [ILLUSTRATIVE] price band" and "the figure shades and labels that region" before any figure is reachable, and neither p. 290 nor p. 291 contains a figure at all (both pages are text-only, including the §16.4 'Measurement' list). evidence: Rendered inspection of PDF pp. 290 and 291 at 150 dpi: no figure, no table, no graphic of any kind on either page; the only figure references present are the unnumbered "the figure" (printed p. 270, twice; printed p. 271, once) and "Fig 16.1" (printed pp. 270 and 271). The figure's own location was not verified in this batch.
acceptance_test: Number the figure (e.g. Fig 17.x) and replace all three instances of "the figure" with that number. Confirm the figure falls on the same page as its first reference or immediately after it, and that the caption states what the reader should learn (break-even band as a region; feasible-volume ceiling; shaded infeasible region) rather than merely naming the diagram.

issue: The range is printed as "(here −6.2–10.4M req/mo)" with a leading dash glyph that reads as a minus sign, i.e. as a negative lower bound. The same range is written correctly elsewhere on the page as "the same 6.2–10.4M band". A reader scanning the figure's axis labels (which presumably show 6.2M and 10.4M) could reasonably mis-read the prose as describing a negative volume.
evidence: Printed p. 270: "the honest output is a range (here −6.2–10.4M req/mo) rather than a single 'the break-even is 7.5M' claim"; three lines later: "the same 6.2–10.4M band reported with Fig 16.1". The two forms are inconsistent within one paragraph.
acceptance_test: Rewrite as "(here 6.2–10.4M req/mo)" or "(here 6.2M to 10.4M req/mo)" so no glyph precedes the lower bound; confirm the figure's axis labels use the same 6.2M/10.4M endpoints.
